producer_report.summary: Athena now removes the target/ of interrupted jobs at the start of every drain and before each run. It also holds a job as an environment stop (low disk) before the producer starts when free space is short. An interrupted job is one the records show as Dispatched, with no registry entry and a free job lock. The sweep calls StateDir::remove_target, so work trees, kept candidates, resume marks and records stay. A job another command is running keeps its target/. New code: disk::reclaim_interrupted_targets plus Athena::reclaim_interrupted, and a Steps::reclaim_interrupted default method that RealSteps implements. Drain calls it at the start of drain_with and before steps.run. The new gate in run/mod.rs produce_and_verify sits after the baseline stage and before the producer's work tree. It runs the existing disk_gate and, if space is still low, returns hold_for_disk. The job is left Dispatched with a hold marker, no candidate and no resume mark. The status shows it as interrupted with the low-disk text, and the producer is never started. Docs updated in disk.rs, drain.rs and close.rs, plus a CHANGELOG entry. Tests added: a core unit test for the sweep, a core test for the pre-producer hold (using a new free-space reader, low_once_baselined), and a drain entry-point integration test. fmt, clippy and the full test suite all passed.

open_issues: A job held before the producer has no resume mark, so a later drain retries it with a fresh plan and producer run, and a retry that is also held before the producer counts toward the drain's usual two attempts. I did not change retry policy (out of scope).
The drain integration test calls drain with a zero budget, so it exercises the drain-start sweep only. The sweep before each run is covered by the core unit test, not by an entry-point test.
mistakes: My first run of the new drain integration test failed because I asserted a sweep log line the test's ui never sees. I removed that assertion; the file and directory assertions are the check.
learnings: StateDir::try_lock_job creates the job directory and job.lock if absent, so a sweep must check target/ exists before locking, or it creates empty directories for jobs that have none.

The free-space hook is a plain fn pointer, so a test cannot capture state. low_once_baselined reads a marker file the baseline check leaves in the job directory (the baseline check runs in <job dir>/baseline).
RealSteps in the drain integration tests writes to its own ui (Quiet in real_steps), so log lines from the drain-start sweep are not visible to a test's Lines.
The baseline checks run after planning, so the new gate sits after baseline_stage.
desires: A way to read a backgrounded command's output file. The path was outside the working directory, so I could only wait for the completion notice.
